title: SDK telemetry check-in: quickstart & samples event hygiene
content:
Context:
Quick sync to align SDK and sample quickstarts telemetry before the next docs refresh. Goal: reduce noise, make onboarding metrics actionable, and prevent event-name churn across SDK languages and the sample apps repo. Meeting was intentionally short (30m) — focus on decisions and owners.

Attendees:
- Maya Hernandez (owner)
- Liam O'Connor (telemetry infra)
- Priya Natarajan (samples repo lead)
- Diego Alvarez (docs + quickstarts)
- Sofia Kim (product analytics)

Agenda:
1) Current telemetry pain points from onboarding flows
2) Proposed minimal event schema for quickstarts
3) Sampling strategy & volume limits for hosted demo keys
4) Action items + short-term rollout plan

Highlights / notes:
- Problem summary: quickstart/sample apps generate many high-cardinality events (full prompt text, per-token logs from streaming demos, unbounded metadata keys). This makes the onboarding funnel dashboards noisy and expensive.
- Product analytics (Sofia) showed that 70% of events labeled "sample_run" contain the prompt body; retention + storage costs ballooned on demo clusters during last campaign. Need to redact/trim by default.
- Liam: telemetry infra can add server-side redaction rules and a lightweight sampling proxy for demo API keys, but we need standardized client-side event naming to make downstream joins reliable.

Decision: adopt a minimal canonical telemetry schema for all quickstarts and sample apps across languages (JS/Python/Go). The schema will be enforced by linters in the samples repo and suggested in SDK starter templates.

Canonical event fields (agreed minimal set):
- event_name (string) -> consistent set documented in CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-telemetry-v2
- event_version (string) -> bump on breaking changes
- sample_id (string) -> short tag of the quickstart (e.g., chat-streaming, embeddings-playground)
- demo_mode (bool) -> indicates interactive demo vs CI-run
- sdk_lang (string) -> js | python | go | other
- latency_ms (int) -> measured client-to-first-byte for generation calls
- tokens_generated (int) -> integer, capped (see limits below)
- outcome (string) -> success | error | partial
- error_code (string) -> optional, normalized
- environment (string) -> demo | e2e | local | production

Privacy and content handling rules:
- Never send full prompt text or user-generated content in telemetry by default. Use a hashed prompt_id if needed for matching to internal eval sets.
- For samples that explicitly show prompt text in the UI (playgrounds), telemetry must indicate demo_mode=true and the client must capture only prompt_length and a prompt_hash (sha256, truncated to 8 chars). No raw text.
- Streaming events: only send summary events (stream_start, stream_end, stream_error) with tokens_generated and first_token_latency. Do not emit every "token" event by default.

Sampling / quota plan for demo keys:
- For any demo_key flagged in telemetry infra, apply 1% sampling for verbose debug events, 100% for summary events.
- For high-traffic public quickstarts (traffic > 1k sessions/day) we will cap tokens_generated telemetry to 1000 tokens per session. Extra tokens will be aggregated server-side into tokens_truncated=true with aggregated_total in periodic batches.

Implementation details / infra changes:
- Priya will add telemetry lint rules to samples repo (.github/workflows/telemetry-check.yml) that fail PRs emitting disallowed fields. Target: lightweight ESLint/Pre-commit hook that flags 'prompt' and 'user_text' fields. (Owner: Priya, due: 2026-11-16)
- Liam will add server-side demo-key sampling and a redaction rule engine (config-driven) that can be toggled per-demo-key. Minimal rollout: staging -> demo -> prod. (Owner: Liam, due: 2026-11-23)
- Diego will update quickstart docs to include the new schema snippet and migration notes for existing samples. Also add a short "telemetry checklist" to the PR template. (Owner: Diego, due: 2026-11-18)
- Maya will prepare a short internal note + product-facing FAQ explaining why we do not collect prompt text and how to collect prompt hashes for debug cases. Draft by 2026-11-12.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we provide a library helper that computes stable prompt hashes (language-agnostic) and include it in SDKs? Pros: avoids copy/paste. Cons: potential misuse. Action: prototyping discussion next week (owner: Priya).
- How to handle customer-specific quickstarts in private deployments where prompts may be required for debugging? Proposal: require an explicit opt-in flag and store those events in separate, enterprise-only retention buckets. Need S&C review. (Tracking: JIRA-DEVEXP-872)

Quick notes to self / rough drafts (informal):
- sample event names draft: quickstart.start, quickstart.complete, quickstart.error, quickstart.token-summary, quickstart.stream-start, quickstart.stream-end
- example small snippet for docs (JS):
  const telemetryEvent = {
    event_name: 'quickstart.complete',
    event_version: 'v1',
    sample_id: 'chat-streaming',
    demo_mode: true,
    sdk_lang: 'js',
    latency_ms: 320,
    tokens_generated: 87,
    outcome: 'success'
  }
  // DO NOT include prompt_text in telemetry; include prompt_hash if needed

Action items (summary):
- Priya: Add telemetry linter + CI check to samples repo. due 2026-11-16.
- Diego: Update quickstart docs & PR template. due 2026-11-18.
- Maya: Internal note + FAQ. due 2026-11-12.
- Liam: Demo-key sampling + redaction engine. staging rollout by 2026-11-23.
- Priya + Maya: Prototype prompt-hash helper library (decide whether to include in SDK seeds). follow-up meeting 2026-11-17.

Post-meeting follow-ups (short):
- I will add the minimal schema to CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-telemetry-v2 and create a short "how to migrate" checklist for sample owners.
- Create a short analytics dashboard template (Sofia) that reads the canonical fields and shows funnel: quickstart-run -> success/error -> retention by sample_id. (Sofia owner, due 2026-11-20)

Notes on tone & rollout: keep messaging clear to new users: we care about privacy and cost; if you need more detailed logs for debugging, we have a documented opt-in path for enterprise customers. For OSS contributors, the linters will help prevent accidental leaks.

Endnotes / links to follow:
- Samples PR with current failing telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/214
- SDK PR with proposed telemetry helper (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/452
- Tracking ticket (enterprise opt-in): JIRA-DEVEXP-872

Raw scratch thoughts (keep here for now):
- Might add a small visualization in quickstart showing "telemetry safe" vs "telemetry unsafe" fields (green/red badges) so contributors can see at glance.
- Consider adding an "example safe event" generator in each quickstart so maintainers can copy a telemetry-compliant payload into analytics consoles.

---
Meeting length: 30m
Next sync: 2026-11-16 (prototype check-in)
